rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.

rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
rules.description: Cookies without the `HttpOnly` attribute set can be accessed by JS scripts, making them more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Detection of Error Condition Without Action
rules.description: Except doesn't do anything and has no comment

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
rules.description: The built-in function 'input' is used which, in Python 2, can allow arbitrary code to be run.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
rules.description: Using a named argument whose name does not correspond to a parameter of the __init__ method of the class being instantiated, will result in a TypeError at runtime.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
rules.description: Using externally controlled strings in a command line may allow a malicious user to change the meaning of the command.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: This reports the external APIs that are used with untrusted data, along with how frequently the API is called, and how many unique sources of untrusted data flow to it.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: Handling general exceptions before specific exceptions means that the specific handlers are never executed.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: When checking a Hash over a message, a constant-time algorithm should be used. Otherwise, an attacker may be able to forge a valid Hash for an arbitrary message by running a timing attack if they can send to the validation procedure. A successful attack can result in authentication bypass.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
rules.description: Building a SQL query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious SQL code by the user.
